memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me. - Deut 5:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before God gives a single command, He reminds Israel who He is and what He has done: "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt." This order matters more than we often realise. God rescued them first; the commandments came after. He did not say, "Keep these laws and then I will free you." He freed them, and then called them to live as a redeemed people. Grace came before obedience — always.

This is the heartbeat of the gospel too. We do not obey God in order to earn His rescue. He rescues us by grace through Christ, and then obedience flows out of gratitude and love. If you have ever felt that God's commands are a burden or a way of earning His approval, remember the order here. Redemption first, response second.

The first command follows naturally: have no other gods. The God who brought you out of slavery deserves the whole throne of your heart. Anything we love, fear, or trust more than Him quietly becomes a rival god. For us, the "Egypt" God has freed us from is sin itself, and Jesus is the greater Deliverer (Rom 6:17-18). Let the memory of His rescue keep every idol off the throne.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I obey God out of gratitude for His rescue, or to try to earn His love?
- What "other gods" quietly compete for first place in my heart?
- How does remembering what Christ has done for me change the way I obey Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You rescued me before I could ever deserve it. Keep me from putting anything on the throne that belongs to You alone, and let my obedience flow from a grateful heart. Amen.
